titel: Why does the apple turn brown?
kurz: Apple slices turn brown in the air, unless you protect them.
bild_im_kopf: Like a bike rusting in the open air: oxygen discolours the exposed surface, and a protective film prevents it.
beobachtung: The untreated slice is brown; the other two stay pale.
erklaerung: An [[enzym|enzyme]] in the apple reacts with the oxygen in the air and forms brown pigments. [[saeure|Acid]] slows the enzyme down; water keeps the air away.
schritte: Drizzle one slice with lemon juice, put one in water and leave one as it is.
